features.title: Start threads in a project on a schedule
features.summary: Work › Automations lists per-project automations and creates, edits, pauses, resumes, runs now and deletes them. A schedule (cron, daily, weekly with an explicit IANA time zone, or every N minutes) starts a new thread in its project with its prompt, agent preset and model through the sessions API. Timing uses DSH's own Schedule domain, so DST gaps are skipped and repeated local times run once; a Host that was down catches up once, for the latest missed occurrence, and a resumed automation starts from its next target. Automations and the last 25 runs of each (trigger, outcome, thread, reason) live in plugin storage and survive Host restarts. Every verb is also an agent tool.
failureModes: An unknown time zone, a malformed cron expression or an interval under one minute is refused at save with the Schedule domain's message.
A project that is no longer registered records a failed run that says to choose a project again.
A missing session-controller records a failed run naming the plugin to add; the schedule keeps its next target.
The Host must be running at the target time; while it is down nothing runs, and at boot each schedule runs once for its latest missed occurrence.
Without the Host plugin the page shows a restart-and-retry message instead of the list.

features.title: Start threads from signed webhooks
features.summary: A webhook automation answers POST /automations/webhook/<id> on the DSH web server. The request must carry x-dsh-timestamp (Unix seconds) and x-dsh-signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>.<raw body>"), keyed with the value behind the automation's secret:ALIAS reference, resolved on the Host per request through the Secret Catalog. Requests more than 5 minutes off, replays inside that window, more than the automation's per-minute limit (and 120 per minute overall) and bodies over 256 KiB are refused. An accepted request starts a thread with the prompt template filled from a bounded, sanitized subset of the request ({{body.path}}, {{headers.name}}, never credential headers), followed by a note that inserted values are untrusted data. Refusals after the automation is found are recorded as rejected runs with what to fix.
failureModes: An unknown automation id gets 404 naming where to copy the URL again.
A missing, malformed or wrong signature, a stale timestamp or a replay gets 401 with how to sign, and a rejected run.
A secret reference that does not resolve gets 503 for the sender and a rejected run naming the alias to fix in Secrets.
A paused automation gets 409 and a rejected run saying to resume it.
Over the per-minute limit gets 429 with Retry-After; the limit is counted before verification so a flood stays cheap, and a flood can delay genuine requests until it stops.
The replay window is held in memory: a request captured less than 5 minutes before a Host restart could be accepted once more after it.
